title: On-call handoff: Evan Brooks (2026-03-03 -> 2026-03-04)
content:
Shift summary (on-call: Evan Brooks)
Date: 2026-03-03 18:00 PST -> 2026-03-04 06:00 PST

Quick summary:
- Quiet first half of shift; primary work was following up on yesterday's memory spikes for model-service-b.
- Received one active alert at 23:12 UTC (see open incidents). Temporary mitigation applied and holding.
- Left a few follow-ups for next shift (see TO-DOs).

Open incidents / ongoing issues:
1) INC-4821: model-service-b memory spikes / OOMs (severity: P2)
   - Trigger: multiple pods in inference namespace restarted due to OOMs when batch size increased during a scheduled load test (external customer).
   - Current state: mitigated. We scaled the HPA min pods to 4 and rolled back batch-size config to 8 (was 16) on the canary route. No new OOMs in last 40m.
   - Temporary mitigation applied: route heavy traffic to model-variant 'redwood-small-v1' via smart-routing policy; disabled burst autoscaling to prevent single-node blowouts.
   - Next actions: run full memory profile when stable; propose quantized variant for this workload.
   - Related artifacts: JIRA-INC-4821, profiling logs @ s3://redwood-logs/profiling/2026-03-03/

2) Token queue length spikes (informational)
   - Observed short spikes up to 120 requests queued for > 30s on route /v1/generate (latency SLO risk).
   - Root cause likely transient: upstream customer load test + small serving pool. Mitigated by temporary route throttling and enabling prefix-KV cache for that tenant.

Actions I took during shift:
- 23:18 UTC: Scaled inference deployment model-service-b to 6 pods (kubectl -n inference scale deploy/model-service-b --replicas=6) and adjusted HPA target to 60%.
- 23:24 UTC: Rolled back batch-size config in config service (config id: cfg-2026-03-03-16) -> set BATCH_SIZE_DEFAULT=8.
- 23:30 UTC: Updated routing policy to route customer-x traffic to 'redwood-small-v1' until profile completed (console -> routes -> customer-x).
- 23:45 UTC: Posted update in #oncall and #infra-alerts with summary and mitigation steps.

Temporary runbook notes (draft) - for model-service-b memory OOMs:
- Symptoms:
  - Pod restarts with OOMKilled
  - Memory usage trending above 90% for > 5m
  - Increased token queue length and tail latency

- Immediate mitigation (fast):
  1) Scale replicas: kubectl -n inference scale deploy/model-service-b --replicas=<n> (start +2 from current)
  2) Reduce BATCH_SIZE: via config service UI or CLI (set BATCH_SIZE_DEFAULT=8 or lower)
  3) Enable fallback routing: set smart-routing rule to prefer a lower-memory model variant (e.g., redwood-small-v1) for the affected tenant/route
  4) Disable burst autoscaling temporarily: update autoscaler policy to prevent aggressive single-node allocations
  5) Notify customer and CS: post brief in #gcs-customer-x (template message: "We're seeing memory pressure; temporarily routing your traffic to a lower-memory variant to keep latency stable.")

- Diagnostic commands:
  - kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --show-labels | grep model-service-b
  - kubectl -n inference describe pod <pod-name> (look for OOMKilled under Events)
  - kubectl -n inference top pod <pod-name> --containers
  - curl -s "${METRICS_SVC}/api/v1/query?query=container_memory_usage_bytes%7Bpod%3D~%5C"model-service-b.*%5C"%7D" | jq '.'
  - Check token queue: console -> metrics -> route:/v1/generate -> 'pending_requests'

- Post-incident follow-up (permanent fixes):
  - Run memory profiler on model-service-b under synthetic load (assign to eng-applied-ml).
  - Evaluate quantized model variant or change model architecture for this workload.
  - Update autoscaler to be workload-aware (avoid single large allocations).

Health checks / dashboards to glance at (links):
- Console: Routes -> customer-x -> metrics (latency, pending_requests)
- Infra dashboard: Inference cluster health (CPU/Memory per node)
- Traces: Jaeger -> filter service=model-service-b -> look for tail latencies
- Logs: Loki -> {job="model-service-b"} -> look for OOMKilled / out_of_memory

Routine checks for next shift (checklist):
- [ ] Confirm no new OOMs in the last 2 hours (kubectl + logs)
- [ ] Verify HPA is stable (kubectl get hpa -n inference)
- [ ] Validate route throttles and fallback are turned off once stable
- [ ] Run a quick smoke test against /v1/generate for customer-x (10 requests) and confirm latency < 300ms P95
- [ ] Start a profiling run (assign ticket) if memory pattern reproduces

Notes to the next on-call (Maya / Noah):
- If you see OOMs reappear, follow the temporary mitigation steps above. Prioritize scaling and rollback of batch-size before touching kernel-level settings.
- I left a draft PR for a config toggle (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/342) to make batch-size change safe during runtime — please review if you have bandwidth.
- Customer-X CS point: @alisha (Slack) informed. They requested an ETA on a permanent fix; tell them we'll have profiling results by EOD if issue reproduces.

TODOs / follow-ups (assigned):
- Evan: upload heap/profile dumps to S3 -> s3://redwood-logs/profiling/2026-03-03/ (in progress)
- Maya: run memprof on canary and share results (blocking: reproduce the load)
- Noah: check autoscaler config and propose policy tweaks (JIRA: JIRA-INC-4821-1)

Misc / Notes to self:
- Remember to add runbook steps to Confluence (link: CONFLUENCE-ONCALL-RUNBOOK) once stabilized.
- Consider lowering default batch size for this model family during high-concurrency windows (customer-specified).

If anything urgent, ping me directly slack @evan.brooks or escalate to SRE lead (pager)

-- Evan
